_comment: Editor UI metadata for MPC B-LEG. Overlaid onto the schema built from BLegConfig (a SosFadeConfig superset). UI ONLY — never touches a trade decision or the source hash. Click Scan Strategies after editing. Params not listed here fall back to their raw field names; the A+ gate params (arm sources, FVG/entry, HTF, veto) are inherited from the A+ bot and still matter because the B-LEG keeps the 'A+ has priority' stand-down — see the A+ strategy's own meta for their descriptions. Labels and descs are shared with indicators/mpc_b_leg_strategy.pine the same way the A+ meta is — label == the Pine input title, desc == its tooltip, changed in the same commit.
edge: The B LEG is the SOS whose retrace arrived LATE. A reversal setup fires its shift-of-structure, but price expands and breaks structure AGAIN in the same direction before it ever pulls back — so the normal A+ leg dies at two-thirds with no entry. On a higher timeframe that is one clean leg, and the retrace does come, just later. The B LEG freezes the Sniper-Zone band (0.382–0.5) of that original break and rests a limit at the 0.5 edge; the tap IS the entry. Stop sits beyond the leg origin (fib 1.0); the target ladder is the broken swing extreme, then the expansion extreme, then a runner. Turned on alongside the A+ engine last night it added significant profit, which is why it was split into its own bot to run in parallel. This is the baseline port — faithful to the Pine — before any of its own entry/stop tuning.

steps.label: 01 · SOS
steps.title: A reversal fires
steps.detail: An A+ shift-of-structure prints and freezes its Sniper-Zone band (0.382–0.5 of the break leg). The B LEG watches that band even though the A+ setup itself is still just armed.

steps.label: 02 · Dies at 2/3
steps.title: It breaks structure again first
steps.detail: Price expands and prints a continuation BOS BEFORE retracing, so the A+ reversal leg dies with no entry (neither 0.5 nor 0.618 was tapped). That death is exactly what ARMS the B LEG on the frozen band.

steps.label: 03 · Late retrace
steps.title: Wait for price to come back
steps.detail: A resting limit sits at the band's 0.5 edge for up to a tunable number of days (bleg_max_days). If price trades back into the band, the tap fills it. If it never comes back, or closes past the leg origin, the leg goes stale and is dropped.

steps.label: 04 · Manage
steps.title: Ladder out
steps.detail: Same machinery as the A+ bot: 30% at TP1 (the broken swing extreme) and stop to breakeven, 40% at TP2 (the expansion extreme) and stop to TP1, then trail the runner.

params.name: bleg_max_days
params.label: Days to watch for the late retrace
params.desc: How long a B leg watches its frozen band for the late retrace before it goes stale. Set in days but counted in bars, so weekends and the daily close do not burn it. 1.25 = the original 120 bars on 15m. Lower means quick retraces only. Sweep 1 to 3.
guide: A band waits longer for a late return

params.name: exec_risk_pct
params.label: Risk % per trade
params.desc: How much of the account each trade risks. Position size is worked back from this and the stop distance, so a tighter stop buys a bigger position at the same risk.

params.name: exec_longs
params.label: Trade longs
params.desc: On = long setups may trade. Off = shorts only.

params.name: exec_shorts
params.label: Trade shorts
params.desc: On = short setups may trade. Off = longs only.

params.name: exec_no_late_day
params.label: No entries in the final hour (16:00-17:00 NY)
params.desc: On = no new entries in the last hour before the daily close. Gold closes 17:00 New York and reopens at 18:00, so this bars 16:00-17:00 New York. It stops trades that get gapped out over the break.

params.name: exec_runner_trail
params.label: Runner trail method
params.desc: How the runner is trailed once TP2 is hit, and which setting below is live. Fixed step is a dollar grid. Structure parks the stop at the last confirmed swing — it breathes with the trend, but a swing lags, so it hands a lot back at the turn. Structure + % ratchet is the default: the same anchor, but the stop climbs one step per step of favourable move. Measured over 6.6 years, that lifted the share of each run actually banked from 43% to 53% on the same 164 trades.
guide: Fixed step — mechanical, worst on a multi-year price range
Structure + % ratchet — measured best on the A+ bot, unswept here

params.name: exec_struct_trail_buf_tk
params.label: Structure trail buffer (ticks)
params.desc: Used by both structure trail methods. The runner stop sits this many ticks beyond the last confirmed swing, so a wick through the swing does not clip it.
guide: Tight to the swing — clipped by wicks
Wide of the swing — survives noise, gives back more

params.name: exec_trail_pct
params.label: Runner ratchet step (% of price)
params.desc: The stop starts at the last confirmed swing and climbs one step of this size for every step of favourable move. A percent rather than dollars because gold ran 1,500 to 3,400 — $20 is a 1.3% trail at one end and 0.6% at the other. Below about 0.5 it starts clipping runners.
guide: Below 0.5 — clips runners, costs real edge
Above 2.5 — barely binds, back to the plain structure trail

params.name: exec_trail_step
params.label: Runner trail step ($ of price)
params.desc: Read by two settings, so it is never greyed out: the fixed-step trail, and the one-trail-step-behind stop floor. On gold 1 pip is 10 cents of price, so 50 pips = 5.0.
guide: Tighter trail — banks sooner, cuts runners short
Looser trail — lets winners breathe, gives back more

params.name: exec_tp2_stop_mode
params.label: TP2 → stop floor
params.desc: What the stop floor becomes the moment TP2 is hit, before the runner trail takes over. TP1 price is tight and can scratch the runner on the first pullback. Breakeven gives it the most room. One trail step behind keeps it under the high-water mark. The trail can still tighten past this floor.
guide: TP1 price — protects the gain, scratches runners
Breakeven — maximum room for the runner

params.name: exec_time_stop_mode
params.label: Time stop
params.desc: Close a trade that has been open for the number of hours below. Before TP1 only is the measured shape: it fires only while the trade has never touched TP1, because touching TP1 moves the stop to breakeven and the trade can no longer take a full loss. Always ignores that and closes on the clock alone, which cuts winners too. Before TP1 only at 36 hours is the DEFAULT as of 2026-08-06, inherited from the A+ fork where it was measured: there it cuts 6 trades, all losers, and takes max drawdown from 8.0R to 5.6R. It has NOT been measured on B legs, which wait for a late retrace by construction, so treat any value here as untested until it is replayed. Off closes nothing.
guide: Off — the clock never closes a trade
Always — the clock closes winners too

params.name: exec_time_stop_hrs
params.label: Time stop (hours)
params.desc: Calendar hours since the fill, weekends included — the same clock the swap is charged on. The 24h-to-40h plateau behind the 36 default was measured on the A+ fork, not on this one. A B leg waits for a LATE retrace by construction, so treat any value here as untested until it is replayed.
guide: Cuts winners as well as losers

params.name: exec_aplus
params.label: A+ has priority (stand the B-leg down)

options.on: A+ stands the B leg down

params.desc: In this fork the A+ setup never places an order — it only holds priority: on a side where A+ would have armed, the B leg stands down. On keeps that gate, so results stay comparable to the parent file. Off lets every B leg trade on its own merit.
